memory_candidates.content: In this repo's /orchestrate multi-task engine, the classifier (orchestrate-triage-classify.sh) already slurps the ENTIRE specs/state.json active_projects array, not just the candidates being classified. A classifier row that needs to reason about a related task's status (e.g. a dependency) can look that other task up from the already-loaded array with zero new reads and zero call-site/CLI changes -- avoid the tempting-but-wrong shortcut of checking membership in the classifier's own CLI candidate list instead, which is a shrinking per-cycle subset (eligible_tasks) in the live path and will not reliably contain a predecessor that has already gone terminal and dropped out of eligibility.

In skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, dispatching a task to research/plan/implement via skill_preflight_update unconditionally overwrites specs/state.json's status field with no precondition check on the prior value (skill_validate_input only rejects the three terminal statuses). This means routing a stale/misleading status (e.g. a discharged 'blocked') to its real phase group requires no separate status-rewrite component -- the dispatched skill's own preflight self-heals the status as a side effect, exactly as the prior researching/planning eligibility convergence already relied on.
